title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-20
notes:
West leads the ♦J against 4♥. West's lead is won by South. Tricks must be lost to the ♠A, ♥A, and ♥K. At first glance, the contract seems to depend on the position of the ♠A.

South can succeed some of the time that West has the ♠A by playing for an elimination. South should cash his other top diamond and cross to the ♣A. Dummy's last diamond is ruffed, eliminating diamonds.

The ♣K should be cashed next and South's last club should be ruffed in dummy, eliminating clubs. South should now exit with a heart. West may be forced to win. If West began with a singleton heart honour or a doubleton ♥A and ♥K, he will be endplayed. A spade return will make the ♠K into a trick while a diamond or club return will yield a ruff and discard.

If West's heart holding allows him to avoid the endplay, South will need the ♠A to be onside.
